reviewer.method: Fresh, from-scratch independent pass over the NEW 60s preview (output/preview.mp4) after the author inserted a new title-card scene ('Pembuka', evidence shot-0..shot-2, 0-15s) at the front of the film and shifted every later scene's absolute timing later by that scene's ~15s real duration. Read output/preview-reference/evidence.json's plan.shots directly for ground-truth shot boundaries (shot-0 0-2.358, shot-1 2.358-11.207, shot-2 11.207-15, shot-3 15-17.718, shot-4 17.718-20.437, shot-5 20.437-24.061, shot-6 24.061-25.843, shot-7 25.843-30, shot-8 30-32.821, shot-9 32.821-39.403, shot-10 39.403-45, shot-11 45-48.564, shot-12 48.564-55.183, shot-13 55.183-60) rather than reusing any absolute timestamp from review/findings-preview-v10.json, whose shot boundaries predate the title-scene insertion and no longer apply. Cross-checked project.json's metadata.scenes (49 entries, filtered to start<60) against evidence.json's shot indices and confirmed a clean 1:1 mapping: scene 'Pembuka' (shots 0-2) = the new title card; scene 'Kebingungan awal' (shots 3-7) = the old opening scene, content unchanged, now starting at 15s instead of 0s; scene 'Memperbaiki pencarian' (shots 8-10) and scene 'Menentukan kegunaan referensi' (shots 11-13) likewise shifted. Read project.json's full shots[0..13].layers arrays (text/image/line coordinates, from/to gates and keyframe arrays) for every shot in scope, and independently extracted frame-exact samples from the CURRENT output/preview.mp4 with ffmpeg (using a select='between(n,a,b)' filter for frame-accurate grabs, not approximate -ss seeking, whenever a single-frame transition needed verifying) rather than assuming the pre-rendered output/preview-reference/shot-N-*.png crops were trustworthy without cross-checking -- in every case checked, those crops' sha256 matched a fresh extraction of the same frame_index from preview.mp4, confirming they are current and not stale. For the title card (shot-0..shot-2), which the task asked to be scrutinized in full: verified the title/subtitle text and colours, the underline draw-in and later shrink-and-disappear sequence frame-by-frame (frames 426-428 of preview.mp4, i.e. 14.2-14.267s, bracketing the authored 14.241s cutoff), the metronome's placement and continuous ticking, the 15.0s hard cut into the old opening scene (frames 449/450, confirmed clean with no bleed-through in either direction), and the welcome line's narration pacing (caption 0.4-3.858s). This surfaced one genuine, reproducible defect not mentioned in the task brief: the metronome's own keyframe data (project.json shots[0] vs shots[1]/[2]) shows its tick rate jumping ~10.7x, from a ~7.1 Hz flutter in shot-0 to a ~0.66 Hz steady tick in shot-1/shot-2, with no narrative event at the 2.358s boundary to motivate it -- confirmed visually via 7-frame tiles sampled at the keyframe spacing on both sides of the cut. Also noted (non-blocking) that the shrunk underline fragment (w=60) persists alone for ~0.73s after the title text disappears, before the 15s cut -- a minor polish point, not a functional defect, since nothing overlaps or clips. For every shot after the title (shot-3..shot-13), content was re-confirmed against project.json's current layer data and either a fresh frame extraction or the current (sha256-verified) output/preview-reference/shot-N-start/mid/end.png for that exact shot, with all times recomputed against this round's shifted absolute schedule -- none were rubber-stamped from v10's now-invalid timestamps. Ran ffmpeg ebur128/volumedetect directly on output/preview.mp4 for full-file and per-segment loudness figures cited in the sound checks below, rather than reusing v10's numbers, since the mix changed with the new scene's added narration and ticking.
